A more precise alternative to this flat dose exists via the STCR targeted-yield equation for wheat cv. WH 542 (Hisar, Haryana -- same Trans-Gangetic Plain agro-climatic zone as Punjab; no Punjab centre exists in the national STCR compilation): FN = 5.65*T - 1.34*SN kg/ha, FP2O5 = 1.91*T - 2.19*SP kg/ha, where T = yield target (q/ha), SN/SP = soil-test available N/P (kg/ha). Source: ICAR-IISS 'Four Decades of STCR Research -- Crop Wise Recommendations', p.92. This equation already combines soil supply and use efficiency into single coefficients (a, b) -- that is exactly why they can't be split into separate soil_supply_factor/fertilizer_use_efficiency terms; use it as a full alternative to standard-dose-plus-adjustment when a per-field yield target is available, not as an additional adjustment on top.
